title: For two centuries, one princely state ruled itself. Then, at noon, it stopped.

sources.text: The Better India - Hyderabad's accession to India, Nizam's rule and its anniversary

caption:
For two centuries, one princely state ruled itself. Then, at noon, it stopped.

At noon on September 17, 1948, the Nizam of Hyderabad broadcast a ceasefire and accession announcement, ending 'Operation Polo' - what Sardar Patel officially termed a 'Police Action' to avoid international intervention.

The campaign, led by Major General J.N. Chaudhari, began September 13, 1948, following an economic blockade and destabilization attempts against the state. Four days later, it was over.

The date is commemorated as Marathwada Liberation Day in Maharashtra and Hyderabad-Karnataka Liberation Day in Karnataka - a reminder that integrating a country isn't one clean signature, it's dozens of separate, sometimes contested, endings.
